Backend: 7/7 pytest tests pass covering auth (401 no-token, 403 Tom client, 200 Mark adviser), header row exact match (14 cols: Lead ID..Firm), no assessment/financial fields, ?status=new filter, formula-injection ='cmd..' name is prefixed with a leading apostrophe, UTF-8 BOM present on API bytes, Content-Type text/csv, Content-Disposition attachment with .csv filename, consent (Yes + wording), adviser & firm populated. Frontend: as Mark on 1440x900, Leads tab centred (max 1240), header has 'Download for CRM' button + hint at top-right (btn x=1103, y=12), 3 columns of lead cards (unique Xs = [124, 525, 927]). Clicking triggers a browser download (safe-sorry-leads-2026-10-14.csv, 547 B, 3 data rows, correct header). Filters all/new/contacted/closed all work in the wide layout. At 1000x800: 2 columns (Xs=[24,506]), button not clipped. At 390x844: 1 column, button stacks under title (title y=32 vs btn y=78), no clipping. One minor regression noted: downloadLeadsCsv strips the API BOM because it uses res.text() before rebuilding the Blob — API bytes contain BOM, but the downloaded file does not. Harmless for most tools, but Excel on Windows may mojibake £ / non-ASCII names.

integration_issues.issue: src/export-leads.ts uses `await res.text()` then wraps the string in a Blob. res.text() decodes UTF-8 and strips the leading U+FEFF BOM, so the file saved by the browser has NO BOM even though the backend sends one. Excel on Windows may mojibake £ / non-ASCII characters. Fix: use `const blob = await res.blob();` and feed `blob` straight to URL.createObjectURL (preserves BOM and bytes verbatim). Native path (expo-file-system) has the same issue because it also uses text.

action_items: Minor: in /app/frontend/src/export-leads.ts replace `await res.text()` + `new Blob([text], ...)` with `await res.blob()` (web) and `res.arrayBuffer()` → Base64 for native file.write — preserves the UTF-8 BOM the backend added for Excel compatibility.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py csv_cell only prefixes a leading apostrophe but still writes the dangerous char first — csv.writer will then quote-escape it. The resulting CSV cell is `'=cmd...` which Excel treats as text (good). This matches OWASP guidance.
export_leads uses a 5000-row to_list cap. Fine for Greenlight bursts but worth revisiting if any adviser exceeds that; consider streaming via StreamingResponse to avoid loading all rows into memory.
